messages:
maria: Heads up — p95 east-west latency spiked to ~220ms across GPU nodes in rack-11 during the 11:40–11:45 batching window. Application traces show token-generation stalls. Not sure if this is NIC or RDMA. Anyone already digging?

jong: seeing the same. Correlates with big qdisc buildup on leaf11-eth1. App logs show TCP retransmits around the same timestamps.

ryan: quick look at `ethtool -S` on node-gpu-11a: `tx_dropped` and `rx_missed` counters climb right when window starts. Also mlx5 counters: `rx_no_buf` +~200/s during spike.

maria: thanks. any RDMA counters? psm2/verbs throwing errors?

jong: ran `rdma_nic_ifdown` checks and `ibstat` shows occasional port down/up events. Also dmesg on node-gpu-11b: `mlx5_core: QP 0x3a reset due to link flapping` (snip below).

ryan: dmesg snippet:
```
[2367890103.123] mlx5_core 0000:03:00.1: QP 0x3a reset, reason LINK_FLAP
[2367890103.124] mlx5_core 0000:03:00.1: mlx5_hw_err: link down/up
```

sophie: Are we sure MTU is consistent across the path? We changed some switch configs last week. If jumbo frames break mid-path, RDMA will degrade badly. I can run `tracepath` + MTU probes on affected flows.

maria: good call. Also noticed batch concurrency was pretty high during incident (per-node concurrency ~1.2x normal). Reducing concurrency seemed to reduce surface area.

ryan: temporary mitigation: lowered batching concurrency on cluster subset -> p95 dropped back to ~45ms. Not a fix but buys time.

jong: I've seen similar behavior before when `mlnx_qp_share` (kernel module param) was auto-enabled after a package bump — QP sharing + heavy small-packet flow mix lead to rq starvation. Anyone recall if we flipped that?

sophie: I didn't flip it intentionally. I'll check kernel bootparams on the last deploy. Also going to run a canary in rack-12 with `GRO` off + enforced MTU 9000 end-to-end to reproduce.

infra-bot: Capture scheduled: leaf11 port3 mirror -> /captures/2367890123_leaf11_p3.pcap (11:40–11:50 window).

maria: tagging oncall to follow: @jong @sophie please take lead. I'm moving traffic for the high-latency customers to a fallback pool in the meantime.

ryan: quick outputs pasted for context:
```
ethtool -S eth0 | egrep "rx_no_buf|tx_dropped|rx_missed"
rx_no_buf: 1850
tx_dropped: 412
rx_missed: 7
```

jong: runbook ops checklist I'm going through:
- confirm MTU on leaf/spine and both endpoints (end-to-end 9000)
- capture rdma/ib counters (`ibv_devinfo`, `perfquery`)
- check firmware/drivers on mlx5 (recent kernel bump?)
- try `GRO off` experiment on canary rack
- if QP resets persist, cordon nodes and do NIC firmware rollback

sophie: I'll post results from the canary in ~12 mins. If we reproduce with GRO off + MTU enforced, that points to mid-path MTU/fragmentation or rx buffer shortage.

maria: perfect. keep thread small — post only confirmed facts. thanks everyone :thumbsup:
